content.text:
The fix is ready. I've updated three functions to use `Math.round()` when converting decimal prices to cents:

1. **`parseEuros` in `money.js`** — handles standard decimal amounts like "39.95"
2. **`cellCents` in `money.js`** — handles spreadsheet imports  
3. **`decimalCommaToCents` in `locale.js`** — handles European decimal-comma format like "39,95"

The root cause was floating-point precision: when 39.95 is multiplied by 100, JavaScript gives 3995.0000000000005 instead of exactly 3995. Rounding ensures we always get whole cent values. All 50 tests pass, and your gym membership now adds successfully!
